_scope: The payroll-tax revenue base in the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Regulations, 2007 (SOR/2007-303). Closes the SEPH question left outstanding by V0.9. Originally owned only the two edges out of fiscal-equalization-program that this provision establishes, with the Territorial Formula Financing parallel and the other publications named in s. 19 recorded as leads. EXTENDED 2026-08-08: mints Territorial Formula Financing itself as a node and closes all seven of those leads — two onto pre-existing seed nodes (statcan-seph, statcan-national-accounts), two onto nodes the 2026-08-07 grok-h1-equalization-named-products.json merge had already built for a different provision of the same regulation (statcan-alcohol-sales, statcan-government-finance-statistics), and three onto new nodes (Census of Agriculture, Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold, Report on Energy Supply and Demand in Canada). All seven citations were re-verified against the consolidated regulation at laws-lois.justice.gc.ca before building.

reports.title: Territorial Formula Financing
reports.description: The federal unconditional transfer to Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut that closes the gap between what a territory could raise on its own and what it needs to provide services comparable to those in the provinces, calculated under Part I.1 of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act and Part 1.1 of SOR/2007-303. The fourth major federal transfer alongside the Canada Health Transfer, the Canada Social Transfer and Equalization, and until this entry the only one of the four with no node in this graph. Its revenue-base formula at s. 19 mirrors the DIVISION 2 Nova Scotia formula at s. 8 term for term in several places (SEPH, the System of Macroeconomic Accounts wage terms, Government Finance Statistics), which is what made this pass cheap once the equalization-named-products cluster had already verified the parallel citations.
reports.cadence_note: Entitlements are announced in December for the fiscal year beginning the following April 1, alongside Equalization, from the same certificate process.

reports.title: Census of Agriculture
reports.description: The quinquennial census of Canadian farms, aligned with the population census years (2021, 2026, ...), producing farm land and building values among its outputs (IMDB record 3438). SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(h) names it explicitly as a publication — 'the value of farm land and buildings in a province or territory ... as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its publication entitled Census of Agriculture' — for the farm sub-base of the Territorial Formula Financing property-tax revenue base, the counterpart to the Nova Scotia division's use of the agricultural balance sheet (CANSIM 002-0020 / table 32-10-0056-01) for the same conceptual measure.
reports.cadence_note: Every five years, in the same years as the Census of Population (2021, 2026); not an annual release.

reports.title: Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold
reports.description: The annual survey of gasoline, diesel, aviation and other petroleum fuel volumes sold by province and territory (IMDB record 2746), reported each year in The Daily as 'Motor vehicle fuel sales'. SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(d)(ii) and s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(A) both name the survey by title for the aviation-fuel and railway-fuel components of the Territorial Formula Financing motive-fuel tax base, distinct from the general fuel-volume definition in s. 1(1) that runs through the fixed table 23-10-0066-01 (statcan-road-fuel-sales) instead.

reports.title: Report on Energy Supply and Demand in Canada
reports.description: Statistics Canada's annual publication (catalogue 57-003-X) reconciling Canadian energy supply and demand by fuel type and province. SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(B) names it as the fallback source for the railway-fuel component of the Territorial Formula Financing motive-fuel tax base, used 'in any other case' where the primary railway fuel tax data is incomplete — the same statutory-fallback shape as the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation's provision for a discontinued Bank of Canada exchange rate.
reports.cadence_note: Published with a lag behind its reference year; catalogue 57-003-X was still being issued as of the 2025 edition. The regulation cites it as a named fallback publication, not as the primary source for this revenue base.

dependencies.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y), the payroll-tax revenue base, makes SEPH a named term in a statutory formula: 'P is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System: (A) the elementary and secondary schools industry group, (B) the hospitals subsector, (C) the nursing and residential care facilities subsector, (D) the provincial and territorial public administration subsector, and (E) the local, municipal and regional public administration subsector'. `calculated_from` because P is a term in the formula, not a consideration — the same test that makes boc-bank-rate calculated_from the policy rate. Note the provision also carves out its own exclusions by NAICS classification, so the edge to `naics` is stated in the same sentence. SCOPE, stated because the section number alone overstates it: s. 8 sits in DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, and defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', which are the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions. SEPH does NOT appear in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5 — the phrase 'payrolls' occurs nowhere in ss. 1 through 8(1)(j), because the 2007 reform folded payroll taxes into the personal-income base. So this is the Equalization Program depending on SEPH through one division of the Regulations, not through the general formula.

dependencies.basis:
MERGED 2026-08-09 (EU/G.73.md): this one edge was defined three times across two slices — twice in equalization-named-products.json and once here — so `npm run validate`'s last-wins load dropped two of the three bases silently, taking two independent statutory citations with them. All three are preserved below; the two duplicate objects were deleted from equalization-named-products.json and this object, the only one carrying a reference_period, was kept.

(a) SOR/2007-303 s. 3.1 (DIVISION 1 definitions) names the framework three times, once for each of three capital-formation aggregates: 'gross fixed capital formation in intellectual property products, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in machinery and equipment, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in non-residential structures, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. Minted 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Q1, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx): the framework is a node in its own right, matching the statute's own wording verbatim rather than an inferred release.
[evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2007-303/page-2.html]

(b) SOR/2007-303 s. 5(b)(i), the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base: 'the portion of the aggregate of corporate profits in Canada, before the payment of income taxes and without any deduction of the aggregate of corporate losses in Canada, that is attributable to any of the 10 provinces for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. A fourth, independent citation of the framework, distinct from the three capital-formation terms in s. 3.1. Minted 2026-08-08, same ruling.
[evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2007-303/page-3.html]

(c) Two further terms of the same formula at SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y) are pinned to the national accounts. 'A is the total wages and salaries excluding supplementary labour income, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts, paid in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, other than the wages and salaries paid by (i) the federal general government sector to employees in the defence industry, and (ii) the provincial and territorial general government sector and the local general government sector to their employees'. And 'M is military pay and allowances, excluding supplementary labour income, paid in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. RESOLVED 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q1): the Regulations name the *System of Macroeconomic Accounts* itself, not a specific release, and Thomas's ruling was to mint the framework as its own node rather than infer a mapping to one of its releases. Target repointed from the inferred statcan-national-accounts (IMDB record 1901, GDP by income and expenditure) to statcan-system-macroeconomic-accounts, which now matches the statutory wording verbatim rather than through a judgement call. This sidesteps, rather than resolves, the still-open statcan-hfce / statcan-national-accounts duplication question recorded in statcan-macro-accounts.json — that question is about which release-level node is authoritative and remains open on its own terms.

dependencies.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(g) is the payroll-tax revenue base for PART 1.1 — Territorial Formula Financing Payments, and it cites SEPH twice, once in each of two formula terms. Term D: 'data on the gross payroll of employers in the province or territory — other than those referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii) of the description of G — for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours'. Term G: 'is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province or territory for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System'.

dependencies.basis: Same provision, SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(g), terms F and H, mirroring s. 8(1)(y)'s A and M. F: 'is the total wages and salaries excluding supplementary labour income, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts, paid in the province or territory in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, other than the wages and salaries paid by (i) the federal general government sector to employees in the defence industry, and (ii) the provincial and territorial general government sector and the local general government sector to their employees'. H: 'is military pay and allowances, excluding supplementary labour income, paid in the province or territory in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. RESOLVED 2026-08-08, same as the corresponding edge from fiscal-equalization-program: target repointed from the inferred statcan-national-accounts to the newly-minted statcan-system-macroeconomic-accounts framework node, per Thomas's Q1 ruling (Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx).

dependencies.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(h), the property-tax revenue base, sub-base B3: 'F is the value of farm land and buildings in a province or territory, measured in current dollars, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its publication entitled Census of Agriculture, and adjusted to exclude farm residences, for the most recent calendar year available in the publication'. The regulation names the publication explicitly ('its publication entitled'), the strongest form of citation this project accepts.

Named twice as a survey by title. SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(d)(ii): 'the number of litres of aviation fuel sold in the province or territory in that year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data from its survey Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold'. And s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(A), for railway fuel: 'in the case where railway fuel is taxed in the province or territory throughout that year and data on the tax is complete and available, by Statistics Canada on the basis of data from its survey Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold'.

SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(B), the fallback where railway fuel tax data is incomplete: 'in any other case, by the Minister on the basis of data prepared by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its publication entitled Report on Energy Supply and Demand in Canada'. An alternative to the Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold edge above, not a duplicate of it — the statute names a primary source and a named fallback publication, the same shape as the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation's statutory fallback for the day the Bank of Canada stops publishing an exchange rate.

SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(f), alcoholic beverage revenues, cites the table three times, once each for spirits, wine and beer. From subparagraph (i): 'the volume of spirits sold in the province or territory in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of table 10-10-0011-01, Value of sales of alcoholic beverages of liquor authorities and other retail outlets, by beverage type (× 1,000)'. Subparagraphs (ii) and (iii) repeat the identical citation for wine and beer. Target node statcan-alcohol-sales was built 2026-08-07 in grok-h1-equalization-named-products.json for the Nova Scotia division's parallel citation of the same table under its retired CANSIM number (183-0024) at s. 8(1)(j); this is the second, independently-verified provision reaching the same node.

SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(b)(ii), the government business enterprise component: 'the product, as determined on the basis of data prepared by Statistics Canada for the purpose of the Government Finance Statistics, of ...'. Target node statcan-government-finance-statistics was built 2026-08-07 in grok-h1-equalization-named-products.json for the identical wording in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5(b)(ii); this is the second provision reaching the same node, and it completes the same chain — a statutory transfer formula through a national statistical programme to the imf-gfsm standard already in the corpus — for the territorial transfer rather than just the provincial one.

_dropped.edge: SOR/2007-303 — how far the SEPH search actually reached
_dropped.why: Recorded so a later pass does not read this as an exhaustive sweep. The phrase 'Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours' was confirmed present at s. 8(1)(y) term P and at s. 19(1)(g) terms D and G — three occurrences in two provisions. Confirmed ABSENT from ss. 1 to 8(1)(j), which includes the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5; the strings 'payrolls', 'gross dollar value' and 'military pay and allowances' all return zero occurrences across that range. NOT SWEPT: ss. 9 to 45, other than s. 19 itself — that covers Revenues to Be Equalized, Simulated Yield, Population, Certificate, Elections, Payments, the rest of PART 1.1, and PART 2 Fiscal Stabilization. Retrieval of the consolidated FullText is capped at roughly 126 KB against a 525 KB document, so whole-document greps on that file are not evidence of absence — this is the same truncation that made the V0.9 SEPH claim unverifiable, and it caught the count above at 'at least three' rather than 'exactly three'.
